svg.title: Eidetic Studio — Patchbay Wiring Reference
svg.text: Samson S-Patch Plus · half-normalled · POWER OFF before touching the rear · photograph after any change
REAR PANEL — looking at the BACK of the unit
Top row = SOURCES (outputs from gear) · Bottom row = DESTINATIONS (inputs to mixer / interface / samplers)
Half-normal per column: rear-top is internally linked to rear-bottom — the rig works hard-wired by default, zero front cables needed.
No speculative runs: 7–8 and 17–18 stay unwired until a real device/need exists — cables go to committed paths only. SC 11/12 is RCA-only — off the patchbay.
DIRECT CONNECTIONS — not through the patchbay
Soundcraft MAIN MIX L/R are XLR outs → PreSonus In 7–8 (rear line ins) · XLR→TRS — NOT In 1–2 (front preamps)
PreSonus Main Out (TRS) → BM9S SAT/SUB IN (XLR) · SAT OUT (HP 80 Hz) → HS8 pair
Vocal mic / DJM-850 REC OUT → PreSonus FRONT In 1–2 · XMAX preamp · recallable gain scenes
Phone / Mac line out → Soundcraft RCA 11/12 · INTERVAL MUTE = instant reference-track A/B
PreSonus USB-C → Mac mini · direct, never via hub · MIDI DIN + USB hub → see sheet 3
TAP (mult): plug into FRONT-TOP — copies the source WITHOUT breaking the rear link.
Dry signal keeps flowing — permanent taps: rows 1/2 front-top → PreSonus In 5/6.
REROUTE: plug into FRONT-BOTTOM — BREAKS the rear link and feeds that destination
from your front cable instead. Use to inject any source into DT/OT inputs.
LISTEN: front-TOP of any column is also a test point for fault-finding a dead channel.
Front-patching = one cable: a source’s FRONT-TOP → a destination’s FRONT-BOTTOM.
⚠ FEEDBACK: keep Aux 1/2 + GRP at ZERO/off on OT channel 9/10 — its output feeds those buses.
PATCH RECIPES — AUX = OT SEND · GRP = DT RESAMPLE · FRONT-PATCH = OVERRIDE

This is the live-performance money patch
Ableton In 7–8: SC summed mix — always
Ableton In 3–4: OT Cue — cue-route the
one element you may want isolated later

Free-running mode C: record LONG takes,
comp the best 8 bars, warp only if needed
Best material comes from reviewing jams,
not from trying to nail it live
Power OFF before any REAR change · front patching is safe live (mute the destination channel first to avoid pops).
Keep labels current · photograph the rear after every change · one cable mystery costs an evening.
